name: AutoFactory Jev Pre-classifier
description: Question set for the optional Jev (TypeSafe AI) pre-classification layer. Each variation holds its questions in model.custom.questions and the prefill confidence bar in model.parameters.minPrefillConfidence. The question NAMES are the contract with the runtime (it reads answers by name); reword or drop questions freely, but keep the names. Messages are unused: Jev has no chat turns, its input is the diff. Only runs when TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set; the auto-factory-jev-mode flag picks shadow or prefill.

risk.instructions: How risky is this change to ship? Score the blast radius of the behavior change, not the line count. Any change to what a customer is charged or shown as a price is at least Moderate.
criteria: Trivial: docs, tests, comments, or formatting only; no runtime behavior change
Low: small additive, isolated change (new endpoint, copy change) with a narrow blast radius
Moderate: modified business logic or shared code with a moderate blast radius
High: cross-cutting change, API contract change, or data migration
Critical: touches auth, payments, pricing/totals, or data integrity

flag_worthy.instructions: Should this change be released behind a feature flag?

criteria.true: It changes user-facing behavior, business logic, an API, or an endpoint, so it should be gated and released progressively
criteria.false: It has no user-facing behavior change (docs, tests, dependencies, config, infrastructure, pure refactor)

pr_type.instructions: What kind of change is this?

criteria.infrastructure: Build, CI, deployment, or infrastructure code

flag_type.instructions: If this change is flagged, which kind of flag fits it?

criteria.release: Temporary flag to roll out new or changed behavior, removed after full release
criteria.kill_switch: Permanent off-switch for a risky or expensive subsystem
criteria.experiment: A/B test of alternatives measured against a business metric
criteria.operational: Long-lived operational control or tuning (limits, timeouts, modes)

flag_action.instructions: Which flag action fits this change? Look for existing flag evaluations around the changed code in the diff.

criteria.create: Flag-worthy, and no existing flag gates the touched code: create a fresh flag
criteria.ride_existing: An existing flag gates this code and the change iterates on the flagged, not-yet-released variation
criteria.extend_variation: An existing multivariate flag gates this code, its variation is already released, and this is an iteration: add the next variation
criteria.child_flag: Net-new functionality inside or next to already-flagged code: create a new flag with the existing one as a prerequisite

feature_novelty.instructions: Is the behavior this change introduces a new path or a change to an existing one?

criteria.net_new: A new path (new endpoint or component) that users without the change never exercise
criteria.incremental: A change to an existing path that both old and new behavior exercise
criteria.mixed: Some surfaces are new, others are changed existing paths

metric_backing.instructions: How should a guardrail metric for this change be measured, given the telemetry visible in the code?

criteria.reuse_event: The code already sends an analytics/track event that measures the affected behavior
criteria.reuse_traces: The affected code is already covered by tracing spans that can back a metric
criteria.ride_o11y: An observability SDK is installed; enabling its instrumentation covers the behavior without new events
criteria.instrument_track: Nothing measures this yet; a new track() event must be added

release_method.instructions: How should this change be released once merged?

criteria.immediate: Turn it on for everyone at once; low risk and nothing meaningful to measure
criteria.progressive: Ramp it up in stages over time without metric-based automatic rollback
criteria.guarded: Ramp it up while monitoring metrics, rolling back automatically on a regression

messages.content: Documentation only (not sent to Jev). Pre-classify a code change for the AutoFactory release pipeline before the agents run: risk, flag-worthiness, change type, flag type and action, feature novelty, metric backing, and release method. Jev reads the PR title, description, changed files, and diff as its state and answers the typed questions in model.custom.questions.
